equity_bridge.item: Investments in associates and joint ventures at book, attributable share (12,356.5 x 58%)
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 segment note 4(b): associates 9,100.9 + JVs 3,255.7; their income is excluded from EBITDA (matching-asset rule); haircut to the ~58% attributable share consistent with the NCI leakage driver

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment: long-run volume growth under China's 45Mt smelting cap plus overseas additions (Guinea refinery, CBA). The equity 5yr CAGR (6.6%) and FCF 5yr CAGR (20%) measure a trough-to-peak upswing (FY2020 EBITDA RMB14.7bn -> FY2025 RMB38.7bn) and are not repeatable; the 3yr revenue CAGR (-6.1%) reflects the deliberate shrinkage of low-margin trading revenue from the FY2022 peak
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGRs (11.3% / 6.6%) diverge by far more than 30% from revenue (-6.1% / 5.3%) and EPS (45.7% / 89.8%): this is a commodity cyclical whose FY2018-20 base years were trough earnings (net income RMB0.7-0.9bn) and whose FY2024-25 end years are an upswing. None of the historical CAGRs is a usable forward growth rate; the scenarios are built on a price-cycle view instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (SBC is 0.02% of revenue, so the two series are identical to the first decimal); interest income is not deducted because the company is net debt. Owner-FCF series (RMB m): FY2018 6,182; FY2019 3,432; FY2020 9,869; FY2021 26,097; FY2022 23,083; FY2023 20,079; FY2024 22,372; FY2025 24,558 -- note these are consolidated (pre-NCI) figures, roughly 58% of which accrue to Chalco shareholders.

scenario_narratives.base: Chalco is valued as a price-taking commodity cyclical at a visible earnings peak. FY2026 earns a record (H1 attributable profit RMB11.9bn, +68%) on aluminium prices up 20-32% YoY while the wholly-owned alumina segment has already swung to a loss. The base case takes FY2026 at its run-rate, then fades the EBITDA margin over FY2027-28 to a 13% mid-cycle level as aluminium mean-reverts and Chinese capacity creep narrows the smelting spread, with the capacity cap, the lean-operation cost base and captive power keeping mid-cycle well above the FY2018-20 trough (8%). Revenue dips 9% peak-to-trough then grows 2-2.5% on Guinea/CBA volumes. The terminal value capitalises mid-cycle attributable owner FCF at 12x, roughly the stock's own current mid-cycle P/E, so no re-rating is assumed. The axes are the aluminium price, the alumina-aluminium spread, Chinese capacity discipline, and how much of the upside leaks to Yunnan Aluminium's minorities.
scenario_narratives.bull: Aluminium stays structurally tight: the 45Mt cap holds, Middle East supply disruptions persist, EV/grid/data-centre demand absorbs the property drag, and the Guinea bauxite quota tightens alumina supply enough to lift the alumina segment back to a modest profit. Mid-cycle EBITDA margin settles at 16% (the FY2024-25 level), CBA and the Guinea refinery add volume from FY2029. NCI leakage is higher because the upside is in smelting, where Yunnan Aluminium's minorities sit.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Goldman view: Chinese smelting capacity creeps past 48Mt, the SHFE aluminium-alumina spread halves by FY2027 and recurring profit roughly halves with it; alumina stays loss-making on chronic oversupply; property demand keeps falling; a Guinean export quota lifts bauxite costs; the Guinea refinery and CBA consume RMB10bn+ of capital at sub-WACC returns. Mid-cycle EBITDA margin 10%, revenue 15% below FY2026, capex committed and not flexing down.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A no-moat, state-controlled aluminium producer whose earnings are the alumina-aluminium spread. The valuation refuses to capitalise FY2026's peak: margins fade to a 13% mid-cycle within three years, the terminal multiple is capped at 12x attributable owner FCF, and 40-45% of group profit is leaked to minorities before anything reaches H-shareholders. Value here is a function of where you think mid-cycle aluminium settles, not of growth. A 15% hurdle on an 8% CNY discount rate demands a deep discount to intrinsic value; expect the entry price to sit well below IV.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin is the dominant assumption: each 1pp of mid-cycle EBITDA margin is roughly RMB2.4bn of EBITDA, ~RMB1.2bn of attributable owner FCF and ~RMB0.8/share (HK$1) of value at the 12x cap
NCI leakage is approximated by a single combined rate; if minorities take 45% rather than 40% of mid-cycle profit, attributable value falls ~8%
Chinese capacity discipline: output already runs above the nominal 45Mt cap; a 48Mt+ outcome is the bear case and shifts weight from base to bear
Alumina oversupply and Guinea policy (81% of China's bauxite imports) can keep the alumina segment loss-making for years, which the 13% mid-cycle only partly reflects
Capital allocation: ~US$1bn Guinea refinery plus the CBA acquisition (not modelled) are overseas bets by an SOE with a governance record of policy-first decisions and frequent management rotation
A/H and FX: the HKD value depends on CNY/HKD 1.1724; the 42% A/H premium means the H-share can re-rate on flows (HSI re-admission June 2026) independently of fundamentals
Dividend policy: a ~40% payout of peak earnings (RMB0.276 interim) will fall with earnings; the market may be anchoring on the peak yield

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX regular close); 52-week range HK$7.09-15.55; FX from Yahoo CNYHKD=X same date; A-share parity from Yahoo 601600.SS
data_sources.financials: 2600.HK_Metrics.csv (FY2018-FY2025 annual, interims to H1 FY2026, CNY millions, from the HKEX annual and interim reports); H1 FY2026 interim report for the 30 June 2026 balance sheet (note 12 borrowings incl. leases, NCI, cash, restricted cash), segment note 4(b) (segment profit, D&A incl. ROU, associates/JVs) and the share-capital table; FY2025 annual report for segment results, impairments, lease payments, other equity instruments
data_sources.qualitative: 2600.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-18): segment dynamics, capacity cap, Guinea/CBA projects, sell-side split (Goldman Sell vs BofA/Citi/MS Buy), governance

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash flow statement, share-based payment expense RMB46.7m (2021 Restricted Share Incentive Scheme); no equity-award taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year); H1 FY2026 RMB7.6m
inputs.buyback_note: Only repurchase-and-cancellation of forfeited restricted shares (RMB2.3m FY2025, RMB1.7m H1 FY2026); an A-share buyback of RMB1,000-2,000m was authorised in 2026 but nothing material has been spent. Count held flat as a modelling convention; SBC is immaterial so the flat count costs almost nothing.
inputs.share_count_basis: 17,154.97m total shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (A + H), from the H1 FY2026 interim report share-capital table; no options or convertibles outstanding, restricted shares already in issue, so fully diluted = basic. Held FLAT; SBC expensed in the flows.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1724 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16). Statements and all flows are RMB; the H-share quote is HKD. Per-share values are computed in CNY and converted at this rate. Parity check: the SSE A-share 601600.SS closed CNY 8.78 on 2026-10-16 = HK$10.29 at this rate against the H-share HK$7.27, i.e. the A-share trades at a ~42% premium to the H-share; that is the normal A/H premium for a PRC SOE, not an FX error, and the H-share price is the one this valuation is compared to.
inputs.net_debt_note: Interest-bearing loans and borrowings per H1 FY2026 note 12: non-current 41,275.0 + current 18,541.7 = 59,816.7, which INCLUDES lease liabilities of 8,957.8 and medium-term notes/bonds; less cash and cash equivalents 43,109.8 (restricted cash 1,176.4 excluded as operating). Other equity instruments (perpetuals) were fully redeemed in FY2025 (nil at 31 Dec 2025), so no perpetual deduction. NCI (RMB55,489.6m at book) is NOT deducted in the bridge because the flows are made attributable-only through the leakage driver (see nci_treatment).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the flows' currency: 10-year CGB ~1.8%; China equity risk premium incl. country premium ~7.0%; levered beta ~1.2 for an aluminium smelter -> cost of equity ~10.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~2.5% (2024-26 MTN coupons 1.6-2.4%, bank loans slightly higher), ~2.1% after tax. Market-value weights ~70% equity / 30% debt -> 7.8%, rounded to 8.0%. No cyclical or SOE premium is stacked on top: cyclicality is charged ONCE, in the flows (mid-cycle margin fade, 30% bear weight, 12x terminal cap). The same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. IFRS 16 lease liabilities (RMB8,957.8m) are inside total_debt and deducted once in the bridge; lease payments (RMB1,484m FY2025, RMB757m H1 FY2026, in financing) are NOT deducted from the flows; right-of-use renewal is covered inside the capex % (held at ~D&A). EBITDA is post-IFRS-16 and D&A includes ROU depreciation, consistent with treatment (A).
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows via a combined leakage driver, NOT a bridge deduction. Non-controlling interests (mainly the ~71% of Yunnan Aluminium not owned by Chalco, plus Ningxia Energy, Guangxi Huasheng, Chalco Shandong and others) took 41.1% of FY2025 profit and 44.8% of H1 FY2026 profit. cash_tax_rate_path is therefore a COMBINED rate = 1 - (1 - cash tax ~18%) x (1 - NCI share ~40-45%): 54% in FY2026 fading to 51% at mid-cycle (bull 53%, bear 48-50% because NCI sits mostly in smelting, which carries the aluminium-price upside). Calibration: FY2025 EBIT 27,478 x (1 - 0.51) = 13,464 vs reported attributable net income 12,674 plus attributable after-tax interest ~2,500 = ~15,200; the ~1.7bn gap is FY2025 impairments (RMB2.0bn PP&E, RMB0.9bn investment property) and disposal losses, which is within non-operating noise and errs conservative. D&A and capex are left consolidated; they roughly offset at mid-cycle (D&A ~ capex), so NCI's share of the net is immaterial.
inputs.equity_bridge_note: Share of profits of associates and JVs (RMB0.6-1.0bn/yr pre-tax) is excluded from EBITDA, so the investments (RMB9,100.9m associates + RMB3,255.7m JVs at 30 June 2026 = 12,356.5) are added back in the bridge, haircut to the ~58% attributable share consistent with the leakage driver. Restricted cash and the trading-book futures positions are treated as operating.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF via the component engine, routed as 'operating company, non-US AND cyclical' (SKILL.md row 2), with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied: CNY-built WACC (a1), CNY flows against an HKD quote with fx_rate bridge (a2), one lease treatment (b), NCI charged once through a leakage driver (c), associates/JVs matched in the bridge (d), SBC rows kept explicit at ~0% (e), risk charged once (f). CYCLICAL FRAMING: base-case margins start at the FY2026 run-rate (H1 FY2026 EBITDA ~RMB33.2bn = 26.5% of revenue, a cycle peak driven by SHFE/LME aluminium +20-32% YoY) and fade over three years to a 13% mid-cycle EBITDA margin, between the FY2021-25 average of 12.4% and the FY2024-25 level of ~15.7% that embedded an alumina windfall now reversed (alumina segment: RMB4.8bn FY2025 profit -> RMB0.8bn H1 FY2026 loss). The terminal value is capitalised on mid-cycle owner FCF, never on FY2026. The 12x terminal cap binds in every scenario (Gordon at 8%/2% would be 17x); 12x attributable owner FCF is roughly the stock's own current P/E on mid-cycle attributable earnings, so the house value embeds no re-rating. SBC-zero: house and street values coincide within rounding; band_position should be read as n/a. Interest income (RMB344m FY2025) is NOT stripped because the company is net debt (RMB16.7bn), so no cash pile is double-counted. Revenue mix caveat: the Marketing segment (~44% of revenue, ~1% margin) means consolidated margin % moves with trading volume as well as metal prices; the mid-cycle margin is anchored to segment profit (primary aluminium RMB20.6bn + alumina RMB4.8bn + marketing RMB1.3bn + energy RMB0.9bn in FY2025) rather than to a ratio alone. Price is a regular HKEX close, not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: The Goldman view: Chinese smelting capacity creeps past 48Mt, the SHFE aluminium-alumina spread halves by FY2027 and recurring profit roughly halves with it; alumina stays loss-making on chronic oversupply; property demand keeps falling; a Guinean export quota lifts bauxite costs; the Guinea refinery and CBA consume RMB10bn+ of capital at sub-WACC returns. Mid-cycle EBITDA margin 10% (FY2021-22 levels plus some cost gains), revenue 15% below FY2026. Capex does not flex down because the overseas projects are committed. NCI leakage is lower (48%) because wholly-owned alumina and smelting suffer together.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +8% (H1 +7.7% with aluminium prices elevated through Q3); FY2027 -6% and FY2028 -3% as SHFE/LME aluminium mean-reverts toward ~US$2,350-2,500/t and alumina stays weak; thereafter 2-2.5% volume growth (Guinea 1.2Mt refinery from ~FY2029, CBA consolidation, EV/grid demand offsetting property)
base.margin_note: FY2026 22.5% = H1 actual 26.5% and an H2 of ~18.5% as aluminium softens off the Q2 peak; FY2027 16%, FY2028 14%, then 13% mid-cycle (FY2021-25 average 12.4%, lifted ~0.6pp for the lean-operation cost base and higher captive-power share). Not the FY2024-25 15.7% average, which carried an alumina windfall since reversed.
base.tax_note: Combined cash tax (~18%) + NCI leakage (~45% FY2026 falling to ~40% mid-cycle) -- see inputs.nci_treatment. The engine labels this 'cash tax'.
base.capex_note: FY2026 3.6% (H1 run-rate RMB3.45bn; RMB5.64bn fixed-asset commitments outstanding); FY2027-29 4.6-4.8% as the ~US$1bn Guinea alumina refinery and energy-saving/green-power upgrades are built; mid-cycle 4.5% ~ D&A (sustaining plus ROU renewal under lease treatment A). The CBA acquisition is an equity investment, not capex, and is not modelled either side.
base.wc_note: Negative capture: receivables + inventories exceed payables for a producer/trader, so revenue growth consumes cash and revenue declines release it (as the RMB7.6bn H1 FY2026 working-capital inflow showed).

bull.narrative: Aluminium stays structurally tight: the 45Mt cap holds, Middle East supply disruptions persist, EV/grid/data-centre demand absorbs the property drag, and the Guinea bauxite quota tightens alumina supply enough to lift the alumina segment back to a modest profit. Mid-cycle EBITDA margin settles at 16% (the FY2024-25 level), CBA and the Guinea refinery add volume from FY2029. NCI leakage is HIGHER here (53%) because the upside is in smelting, where Yunnan Aluminium's minorities sit.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 is for compounders; this is a commodity cyclical valued at an earnings peak. Bear raised to 30% because the bear case is the published view of a major house (Goldman, Sell), the alumina segment is already loss-making, China's capacity cap is already being exceeded through 'creep', and the base case itself depends on the cap holding. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: aluminium staying at peak, alumina recovering, and the overseas projects (Guinea, CBA) earning their cost of capital under sovereign and regulatory risk. Base 50%: the mid-cycle fade is the central expectation of the BofA/Citi/Morgan Stanley camp as much as the bear camp; the two differ on how far and how fast.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
